correctness.rationale: For any nonempty noncomplete confidence graph, a mixed-adjacency triple yields six explicit rates and forward/reverse products u²(u+v) versus u³. Positivity of noise proves finite irreducibility; the violated Kolmogorov criterion proves stationary nonreversibility. For q=1 complete social contacts, an explicit rising-factorial stationary law verifies each detailed-balance pair in the fully compatible case, and uniform independent flips verify the empty case. Exact rational generators validate the K2 stationary vector and both currents; analytic strict concavity on (0,1/2) and negative derivative thereafter prove unique maximum. 1479 independent exact checks passed; finite checks do not certify the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The original 2022 paper supplies the stochastic rule and studies mean-field stationary concentrations and bifurcations; its inspected Model/Results do not state or imply the full finite-configuration cycle-affinity and confidence-graph classification or exact two-agent entropy-production law. The 2021 bounded-confidence predecessor has a different independence step restricting extreme transitions, and later general nonequilibrium methods do not themselves compute the model-specific sharp classification. Actual published-record searches and accessible historical claims disclosed no stronger covering statement, while hidden general coverage remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: General reversibility/entropy-production theorems for noisy interacting particle systems may encompass some claims without using q-voter terminology.
Publisher full article access was partly rate-limited; comparisons were made against indexed substantial sections, rather than every appendix page.
The two-person count-chain formula alone does not imply analogous EPR expressions for arbitrary population sizes, q, or networks.
The 2021 closely related paper has different independent update constraints; any overlooked revised formulation merits independent verification.

value.rationale: In the motivating three-opinion q-voter process, all labels receive unbiased spontaneous resampling yet partial confidence breaks steady-state detailed balance. The graph- and q-independent obstruction determines when this mechanism is unavoidable; its converse for q=1 on complete social contacts is a natural exact classification across all confidence graphs. The exact smallest-population EPR and its unique intermediate-noise optimum quantify a physically meaningful nonequilibrium observable, even though the mean-field concentration equations describe stationary equilibria. This exceeds a routine restatement of a general Markov criterion because the structural opinion-compatibility dichotomy and model-specific exact rate/current expressions are derived and sharp.
